raw_response:
I am an old hand at this now. I cannot chase fancy ways. I look at what my land did before, what the others around me are doing, and how much cash I can spare. With only 9 mu and some people working outside, I have to keep things steady. Wheat and maize are still my main insurance, because even if one side is not so good, the other can still bring grain and money. Cotton I keep on a small piece because it can bring cash if the year is decent, but it needs more watching. Mungbean I only keep on a little land because it is cheaper to manage and does not ask for much water or fertilizer.

For the wheat-maize land, I will keep 5 mu in the usual double crop. I do not want to cut too much fertilizer, because if wheat turns yellow or maize grows thin, the loss is worse than spending a bit more. But I also cannot throw money around, so I use round amounts, mostly like I used last year. Cotton and mungbean stay on the other 4 mu. Cotton gets some fertilizer and a couple of irrigations if it stays dry. Mungbean I manage lightly, mostly to save money and spread risk. Family labor I use first, and only hire a little when work piles up.
